published.citation: Chen et al. 2014, dayside brightness temperature at 1.22 µm (NASA Exoplanet Archive emission table): 2996 +/- 261 K, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014A%26A...563A..40C/abstract

temperature.note: Its day side's brightness temperature is measured in secondary eclipse at 1.22 µm (European Southern Observatory (ESO)/Max Planck Gesellschaft (MPG) 2.2m Telescope at La Silla Observatory GROND) and nobody has imaged it, so the color is a Planck spectrum at its published temperature.
temperature.chosen: 2 measured of 5 rows; the smallest relative uncertainty, then the longest wavelength
temperature.facility: European Southern Observatory (ESO)/Max Planck Gesellschaft (MPG) 2.2m Telescope at La Silla Observatory GROND
